newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks lower; await Fed policy decision.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks lower; await Fed policy decision.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks were lower Wednesday as Wall Street stayed cautious ahead of the outcome of the Federal Reserve's policy-setting meeting, even as most analysts predicted no change in interest rates.
At 1 p.m. EDT/1700 GMT, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 19.91 points at 7,702.42.
But in the broader market, advancing issues led declines 15-10 on modest volume of 286 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite rose 9.84 points to 1,448.09.
The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee -- the Fed's policy arm -- was expected to announce its verdict on monetary policy around 2:15 p.m. EDT/1815 GMT after holding a two-day meeting.
"There's some caution ahead of the Federal Reserve announcement," said Hildegard Zagorski, an analyst at Prudential Securities. "There's not too much exuberance."
The blue-chip market shifted restlessly between positive and negative ground for much of the morning session.

"The market has been all over the place," said Alice Hook, first vice president and trader at McDonald & Co. "There is some caution ahead of the FOMC, just in case they raise rates. ... It's fairly volatile."
Analysts also said the Dow index was pulled lower by weakness in some of its 30 stock components.

"Shares of AT&T and Disney are off sharply, so much of the Dow's fall is internally related," said Harvey Hirshhorn, chief economist and investment strategist at Stein Roe & Farnham. "Cyclicals are a little weaker as opposed to the S&P."
AT&T was down 1-1/4 at 35-1/8 while Disney's stock lost 1-15/16 to 76-5/8.

Italy's STET/Telecom Italia said it was entering a strategic global telecommunications alliance with AT&T. AT&T President John Walter said it was too early to talk about taking an equity stake in STET.

Disney was lower after brokerage house Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said it downgraded the company's stock due to concern that Disney's ABC unit would fall deeper into third place in ratings in the upcoming TV season.
